column3: Close to the Hebrew; “the pupil of your eyes” is rendered “the apple of your eye.”
Close to the Hebrew; וּמֹדָע (“a kinsman”) is rendered “your nearest kin.”
Close to the Hebrew; “a strange woman… a foreign woman” is rendered “the immoral woman… the seductress.”
Close to the Hebrew; וּנְצֻרַת לֵב (“wily of heart”) is rendered “a crafty heart.”
Close to the Hebrew; “she made her face strong” is rendered “With an impudent face.”
Close to the Hebrew; “the man” is rendered “my husband.”
Close to the Hebrew; לְיוֹם הַכֵּסֶא (“the full moon”) is rendered “the appointed day.”
The second line is difficult (“like an anklet to the discipline of a fool”); NKJV renders “as a fool to the correction of the stocks.”
Close to the Hebrew; “numerous are all her slain” is rendered “all who were slain by her were strong men.”
Close to the Hebrew; דַּרְכֵי שְׁאוֹל (“of Sheol”) is rendered “to hell.”
